draft.briefing: Hey, you're in Ponnani! This town where the Bharathappuzha meets the Arabian Sea was once called the 'Little Mecca' of Malabar, a centre for people seeking knowledge.
draft.hungryLine: Haneena Restaurant, by the big pond near the old masjid, is famous for mutta pathiri and beef fry.

moodReplies.show-me-around: Misri Masjid is an 8 min walk and Valiya Juma Masjid about 9 min. Ponnani Lighthouse stands on the south bank of the river.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Take the jankar ferry ride across to Tirur, or walk the hanging bridge at Biyyam Kayal.
moodReplies.surprise-me: Misri Masjid means Egyptian Mosque. It was built in the 1500s for the army of Zainuddin Makhdoom, who came from Egypt to help the Zamorin fight the Portuguese.

legends.title: One of 108
legends.body: Thrikkavu is considered one of the 108 Durga temples consecrated by Lord Parasurama in Kerala. Its name is believed to come from 'Thrikkani Kaadu'.

legends.title: Little Mecca
legends.body: Ponnani was once called the 'Little Mecca' of Malabar, and this mosque was the headquarters of those seeking knowledge. A madrasa still sits in its grounds.

tips.title: Dress modestly near mosques.
tips.body: The old town around you is full of mosques, so cover shoulders and knees.

tips.title: Ride the jankar.
tips.body: The Ponnani ferry crosses to Tirur and gives you the estuary from the water.

story.title: The big mosque
story.body: Ponnani Juma Masjid was built in the year 925 of the Hijra calendar. Historian William Logan mentions it in his Malabar Manual.

story.title: Help from Egypt
story.body: Misri Masjid was built for Zainuddin Makhdoom's army, who came from Egypt to fight the Portuguese alongside the Zamorin. It's a remnant of old trade between Egypt and the Malabar coast.

story.title: A temple turned depot
story.body: Tipu Sultan's army turned Thrikkavu Temple into an ammunition depot. The Zamorin later repaired it.

story.title: Lights on the estuary
story.body: A steel mast with an oil wick went up in 1937, then a gas flasher in 1948. The present 30 m lighthouse was commissioned on 17 April 1983.
